title: observability: token/KV cost+latency breakdowns, dashboards, tracing spans, and alert tuning
author: Priya Desai
description: Motivation: We've seen several incidents where tail latency and unexpected token-level cost increases were only visible after customer escalation. This PR adds token-level cost and latency breakdowns across the serving stack (request, batching, KV cache, model execution), improves KV cache hit/miss metrics, surfaces KV span tracing for hot paths, and ships a curated set of Grafana dashboards and alert tuning to reduce noisy alerts and catch regressions early. What this changes: 1) Metrics: introduce metrics/redwood_token_cost_total and redwood_token_latency_seconds with labels {model, route, customer_tier, kv_hit}. Add KV-specific metrics: redwood_kv_cache_hit_total, redwood_kv_cache_miss_total, redwood_kv_cache_latency_seconds. 2) Tracing: add spans for KV lookup and cache population with tags for key namespace and approximate token_count; instrumented in serving runtime and python/ts SDK adapters. 3) Dashboards: new Grafana folder observability/token-level that includes cost/latency heatmaps, KV hit-rate panels, per-route token-cost breakdown, and an SLO dashboard for 99th-percentile token latency. 4) Alerts: tune two existing alerts to use adaptive thresholds based on baseline percentiles and add a new alert for KV miss-rate regressions (>5% delta sustained for 10m). 5) Rollout: feature-flagged metrics/tracing enabled by default for internal clusters; customer-facing rollout behind org-level opt-in. Testing & validation: unit tests for new metric emission logic, integration test that simulates KV hits/misses and asserts metrics/traces show up in test collector, manual verification of dashboards in staging. Backwards compatibility: metrics are additive and guarded by feature flags; no breaking API changes. Linear/Jira: addresses ENG-2890 and ENG-3021, support follow-up SUP-512. How to review: focus on metric labels (avoid cardinality explosion), verify trace span boundaries are minimal, and confirm dashboard panels map to new metrics. Release notes: Adds token-level cost/latency metrics, KV cache metrics, tracing for KV operations, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts to reduce noisy pager storms. Rollout plan: merge to main, enable in staging for 48h, run canary against 5% of traffic, then gradually opt-in customer orgs over 2 weeks. Contact: @priya for follow-ups and instrumentation questions.

review_comments: Ana Gomez: overall looks good. Concern: label cardinality on route+customer_tier+model+kv_key could explode. Please confirm we cap kv_key or hash it.
Priya Desai (author): we hash kv_key to a fixed-length label and added label_sanitizer to metrics.py (see tests). Updated tests to assert hashed label format.
Liam O'Connor: can we avoid tracing span overhead on hot paths? Are spans sampled or dropped under high QPS?
Priya Desai (author): spans are low-overhead and sampled by default. Added a config param tracing.kv_span_sample_rate with default 0.01 and a circuit-breaker to skip spans if latency budget is tight.
Jae Park: alert tuning looks reasonable but recommend moving to adaptive thresholds based on 7-day baseline rather than static thresholds to reduce noise.
Priya Desai (author): switched the alert rules to use percentile_baseline metric helper (7d window) and added a fallback absolute threshold for small-volume routes.
Ana Gomez: approved after label and sampling clarifications.
Liam O'Connor: approves. Left a minor comment about documenting the feature flag in release notes.
Release CI: all checks passed on the final run (lint, unit, integration, canary smoke).
release_notes: Adds token-level cost and latency metrics, KV cache hit/miss metrics, KV tracing spans, Grafana token-level dashboards, and tuned alerts for KV miss-rate regressions and token-latency P99. Adds feature flag for staged rollout and docs on interpreting token-level diagnostics.
